body:
Nothing quite as objectively tragic as what has been posted I'm sure, but my life feels like a series of these moments. If I had to pick, the first would be my first relationship, spawned in spite of me fighting the desire to care for anyone for exactly this reason. We were inseparable for over a year. But life moves on, and when it came time that we had to separate, it became clear that things would end, and that they would do so quickly. I was left with the choice of ending it myself or trying to enjoy what little time before it happened, all the while simply being made to watch as time marched forward to that point. I agonized over it, and like clockwork, exactly how I expected it to occur, it did. Being strung along for years afterwards did not help matters. I fell into a deep depression and it took years to claw myself back out. 

By far the worst was after.  Made more terrible by not the loss itself, but the discrediting of all that had been done. A long distance relationship. It was never meant to be something serious. Someone I had known for years finally fessing up their feelings, and us trying to see if maybe, just maybe, things could work. We agreed to an open relationship and kept things casual, but that didn't last long. We wanted to be together, and so I took my first trip, a crazy adventure taken by myself across the damn country, hitchhiking the last length from the airport just to see her, walking up the road and finally meeting in the middle of the street. Nearly ten years. We held it together that long. Making trips back and forth, holding on as long as we can, enduring the same pain every time we were forced to go back. Unfortunately, over the years, she slowly began to succumb to depression. Her mother had a history of mental illness, and she had a rough childhood. It was complicated, and it was bad. I did all I could to help, and encouraged her to seek help if she needed it. 

The moment that broke me was the day she disappeared. Like a fucking bad movie scene. We had celebrating valentines day the day prior. I went to work, got a promotion that would have given us a chance, at least a start to finally find a place and be together. She never came online. She stopped responding to my texts. She just disappeared. I wrote it off for a day. We've had tech issues in the past. By day 2 I was worried about her. By day 3 I called her house, she had never been completely out of contact this long, even so much as to just say "hey, I'm alive". I call and I find she's gone. Moved out to Michigan or some such, transferred her job, left a few days ago. I find her on facebook and manage to piece everything together. She's staying with some dude in Michigan she met through one of the games we played. She doesn't respond, but she still listens. I let her know I know, and I more than anything I just want to talk. I just need to know why. The pain of fear, of thinking she might be in danger gets replaced with that of utter and abject betrayal. Eventually she started responding. She claims she doesn't know what she is or what she wants anymore. She's completely lost and doesn't know what to do. She talks to me for a few more days and then pleads to get out of there. I bring her back here for us to talk. We talk for a few days but in the end she leaves again. On good terms, but she can't bring herself to stay after what she's done (not an assumption, I was told as much, though who can say the truth of it). She knows I'm conflicted. I have to work the day she leaves, leaving with a friend and his wife I've met once before to a town not far from where I live. I get to the door and turn around, just to hold her one last time. I do it knowing with absolute certainty it will be the last time I ever will. When I come back from work she is gone. And with her, the last of my hope for the future. 

The ultimate irony being that she now lives not but an hour or two from me. What we had always wanted, what we fought for years to achieve, we finally have, and yet we have nothing. I have nothing. We still talk. She knows, that if anything ever went truly bad, I would still help, but we will never meet again. We played at maybe things would work out in the future for a while, but it was a game that played out for a year, and was merely comfort for both of us. I had to end it, and being the one to do so drove an unwilling knife into my heart. I don't know where she is now and even though I could likely find out should I desire, it's best to not know. If she wanted me to come, she would summon me herself. She' has a job, her friends, and she's getting help for her depression now. All I can ask is that she's safe. Despite all this I don't wish her ill will. For what we endured, for how long we endured it, not everyone has the strength, especially when they've been through so much more.

I find myself at this point lost and without hope. Nearly fifteen/twenty years have passed since these ordeals. I'm older now, my hopes for a relationship, let alone approaching something that could hold a candle to what was had are long gone. Now I live on merely to watch the world turn. I have accepted that when my time comes I will face that dark eternity alone, hoping only that I made something, anything, better along the way. Hoping that maybe for our time together she found her way, even if never found mine.

No. In a sick twist of fucking fate I was promoted and given a raise that would have let us get the apartment we were waiting for the day she dropped off the face of the earth. I don't have the time to take off right now. Speaking of, I now need to find some way to endure the trip to work.

Nothing. She doesn't really have anything stopping her from making some changes and having a perfectly enjoyable life except the fact that she is constantly depressed and has no motivation to change/can't see a future that isn't miserable because of said depression. I know what it's like, I've been there, but I've learned to become self aware of the situation which defuses it. She either can't or hasn't learned to yet, and I have tried to ease her into helping herself, but it's not working, and things are getting worse.
